initial_distinct_hypothesis: Using the input parameter as the mask or start-index destination, while retaining its original direction value in a local, may change allocator coalescing. Both variants regressed. Unsigned mask and register storage specifiers did not improve allocation.
second_hypothesis: Array address-expression shape may change compiler-generated induction temporaries. Flat indexing, direct field accesses, row locals, explicit outer cursors, commuted pointer addition and byte-address expressions did not improve the frontier. These are not the previously rejected explicit inner pointer-induction variant.
successful_hypothesis: The observed neg/or/srawi/andc sequence is compiler lowering of a conditional constant selection, rather than explicit source-level bit operations. Writing int start = direction ? 0 : 3 gives the compiler an unnamed conditional temporary; it produces the exact retail allocation. Both declaration-initializer and separate-assignment spellings measured 100%. The initializer is retained.
method: Each variant replaces only the target source, builds its object through canonical Ninja, and measures it against the existing retail split using objdiff. Variants are discarded; final verification rebuilds the retained source and compares canonical and relocation-strict results, ELF text bytes and relocation tuples, then the entire linked DOL.
